prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); proposes initial TOBT (Target Off Block Time). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; flags imbalancing TOBTs); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; applies Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate for feasibility; no safety judgments); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT (Calculated Takeoff Time) from runway metering, departure fix loading, sector loading, GDP rules); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; shows values with confidence status, last update, reason code; Common Situation Display shows agreed targets as proposed/under negotiation/frozen/exempted); Tower Sequence Manager (runway sequence; flags CTT vs local order; receives CTT from Departure Metering Service); Arrival Regulation Console; Ramp Movement Board (milestone timestamps, apron constraints, to Audit Event Ledger); Time Synchronization Service (reference clock, timestamps); Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR; exemptions, priority codes, fairness metrics); Collaborative Decision Log (records challenges, counterproposals, acceptances, rejections, reason codes for TOBT/CTT); Contingency Operations Console; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Airline Interface Adapter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Digital Briefing Room; Flight Data Exchange; Alert Distribution Hub; Identity Access Service; North/South Runway Meter; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin; priority policy); Slot Coordinator (call sign Halcyon; runs allocation, reviews CTT, requests adjustment, logs exemptions); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron; reviews TOBT; shall confirm operator TOBT revisions in Portal before freeze horizon); Ground Handling Dispatcher (handling milestones as negotiation inputs until freeze); Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline; assesses off-block pattern; Stand Tow Request Form); Tower Supervisor (Brindle; may challenge CTT); Aircraft Operator Representative; Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Items: TOBT, CTT, delay slip, Tactical Regulation Proposal, GDP status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, duty coordination alert, Slot Compliance State, reason code. Negotiation collaborative outside freeze horizon; accepted amendment replaces prior value. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode, Recovery Phase (shorter

Document units:
S268: At the configured freeze horizon, the Regional Flow Platform locks the Target Off Block Time unless a rule-based exception or an authorized operational override is recorded.
S269: A frozen Calculated Takeoff Time may still be revised when the Slot Allocation Engine receives a capacity update that changes the feasible departure allocation for the affected traffic set.
S270: When a frozen value changes, the Airport CDM Portal requires a revised reason code and marks the earlier value as superseded rather than deleted.
S271: The Audit Event Ledger stores the previous value, new value, responsible user or automated function, timestamp, authority basis, and applicable operating state for every target time change.
S272: The Identity Access Service ensures that only users with the assigned operational role can approve frozen-time changes, manual exemptions, or retrospective corrections.
S273: The Data Governance Steward reviews audit samples to confirm that timestamps are complete, reason codes are valid, and manual changes can be traced to an operational justification.
S274: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses frozen targets, actual milestone timestamps, and audit records to measure compliance, delay attribution, negotiation effectiveness, and rule quality after operations.
S275: The tower sequencing function translates the frozen operational targets from the regional flow process into an executable runway order for departures at Meridian Regional Airport.
S276: In this section, Tower Sequence Manager is also called Ironleaf for tower sequencing discussions.
S277: The Tower Supervisor is the operational owner of the departure sequence and uses the Tower Sequence Manager to confirm that each flight can be advanced without creating unsafe surface compression.
S278: The workflow starts when the Flight Data Exchange provides current flight intent data and the Departure Metering Service aligns each Target Off Block Time with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time.
S279: The Tower Sequence Manager then builds a provisional order by runway, departure fix, aircraft wake category, and locally configured spacing rule.
S280: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter maintain separate queues, but the Tower Supervisor can view both queues together when runway balancing is required.
S281: The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms whether an aircraft is still at stand, entering the movement area, holding short, or already committed to the departure stream.
S282: The East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor improve queue accuracy by detecting aircraft movement before manual ramp status updates are available.
S283: The Ramp Control Lead coordinates pushback release priorities against stand conflicts, taxi lane constraints, and the runway demand visible in the Tower Sequence Manager.
